ledger.claim: The artifacts describe one and the same trip, which is the rider's threshold identity showing under POL-RD-08(a): trip_id TRP-00514 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the clock runs consistently across them — the trace's first fix at 2026-09-02T10:36:40+08:00 matches trip_record.started_at, and its last fix at 10:58:40 matches trip_record.ended_at. No artifact's timestamps run backwards and no two admitted artifacts disagree by anything approaching 10 minutes.

The governing distance measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which POL-RD-01 makes controlling wherever it disagrees with trip_record.actual_distance_km (the record's 11.8 km is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test). The trace measures 11.75 km of driving against a booked optimal of 5.1 km, an excess of 6.65 km.

Both establishment limbs of POL-RD-01 pass, and the clause requires both: the excess is 130.39% of optimal_distance_km, far above the 20% limb, and 6.65 km in absolute terms, far above the 0.8 km limb. Nothing in the rider's own conduct or profile reduces the excess, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The excess of 130.39% also exceeds 50% of optimal_distance_km, so POL-RD-01 makes this an additionally MATERIAL deviation and triggers the driver_profile check in POL-RD-06. On that check the driver carries deviation_flags_90d of 0 across completed_trips_90d of 250, so no repeat pattern is established and the rider claims the arithmetic POL-RD-02 refund, not the POL-RD-06(b) uplift. The materiality itself rests on this trip's own trace alone, which is where POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 require it to rest.

No traffic advisory supports the driver's 'the direct road was heavy' explanation. The advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00514-01 is MISSING — status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and its own note records that no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window. A MISSING artifact carries no fact and can carry no fact, but its absence is itself citable, and it means POL-RD-03 cannot be run at all: there is no advisory naming a road, expressway segment or junction the optimal route traverses, and no validity window to overlap the trace. The driver's bare assertion in the counterparty statement is exactly the general 'traffic was bad' assertion POL-RD-08 says does not discharge his burden.

There is no rider-requested detour to exonerate anything. The chat log EV-CHAT-00514 contains zero messages over the whole trip, so no rider instruction was ever recorded, no waypoint_hint exists to test, and POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record. Under POL-RD-08 the driver must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to excuse the excess; he has named none.

Nor did either endpoint move. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null on the trip record, amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, and there is no chat log in which a different address could have been given. POL-RD-05 therefore cannot re-baseline this trip against amended endpoints, and the extra kilometres the rider paid for are not an amendment effect.

This was not a shared ride. vehicle_type on the trip record is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the baseline for the threshold test is the ordinary optimal of 5.1 km rather than any inflated matched-itinerary figure; solo_optimal_distance_km is null and irrelevant here.

The distance-refund route is open to the rider because POL-RD-11 does not bite: the fare breakdown records fare_model METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, so this was not an upfront-quoted trip and POL-RD-02, not POL-RD-11, governs the remedy. The rider was billed by the metre for a detour he never asked for.

The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 as well as under the admissibility pre-pass: coverage_pct is 100.0, there are 133 fixes at a 10 s sampling interval identical to the expected 10 s interval, gaps is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0. No limb (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 is met, so no independent corroboration is required and the deviation stands on the trace alone.

Running POL-RD-02 on the metered fare the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary: charged_total is 19.61; recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 5.1 km + 0.28 x 9.0 min) x 1.0 surge multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo = 10.945; refund = 19.61 - 10.945 = 8.665, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 8.70 to the rider. That is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and at 44.2% of charged_total it is far below the 90% share that would convert the outcome to FULL_REFUND, so the ruling on this rider-filed dispute is PARTIAL_REFUND with the balance of the charge left in place.

No pass-through line distorts that computation in either direction: the fare breakdown's erp_lines total SGD 0.00, tolls_erp is 0.0 and there is no airport surcharge, so the whole contested 19.61 consists of base, distance and time charges — precisely the lines POL-RD-02 recomputes and the lines the rider overpaid. No POL-RD-09 correction is due, and none is claimed on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

The rider's own profile gives no ground for demanding more of him than the trace he has produced: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 premium-corroboration trigger — 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated — is not engaged, and the claim stands proven on the gps_trace alone.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern that could uplift the remedy against the driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, a ratio of 0.00, short of the 0.05 threshold that POL-RD-06 pairs with its 40-trip floor. No pattern being established, POL-RD-06(b) does not convert the POL-RD-02 partial into a FULL_REFUND of charged_total even though this trip's excess is material, and POL-RD-06(c) adds no driver-conduct referral. The two profile counters are cited only for the test POL-RD-06 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

The driver's exposure is bounded by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic, not by the rider's demand. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs, and the surge_multiplier is 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 5.1 optimal_distance_km + 0.28 x 9.0 optimal_duration_min) x 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee = 10.945, against a charged_total of 19.61. The refund is 19.61 - 10.945 = 8.665, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 as 8.70, which is 44.19% of charged_total and far below the 90% share that would make it a FULL_REFUND. The rider's demand for the entire 19.61 has no basis in the recomputation; the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND and no more.

Nothing may be added on top of that refund. The fare_breakdown carries no erp_gantries, tolls_erp of 0.00, airport_surcharge of 0.00 and an optimal_route_erp of 0, so there is no off-route or phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge to correct under POL-RD-09. The POL-RD-02 figure of 8.70 is therefore the driver's total liability on this trip and no pass-through correction is due in addition to it.

The driver does not contest that the deviation is established on the trace, and he cannot invoke POL-RD-03: the traffic_advisory on which that exoneration depends is absent from the pool. EV-ADVIS-00514-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and fired issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window), and under POL-RD-08 a bare assertion that traffic on the direct road was heavy, citing no advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden. The record therefore decides the case on the remaining clauses and the matter is confined to the bounded POL-RD-02 remedy above; the driver asks for that remedy and nothing wider.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this was a real, unexcused detour, and the fare is recomputed under POL-RD-02. The distance-and-time lines are refunded; the rest of the charge stands.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00514 (weight 1.0) is complete and unimpaired — 100% coverage, 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0 — so none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met and the deviation stands on the trace itself. The trace measures 11.75 km of driving against a booked optimal of 5.1 km. The trace figure governs over the trip record's rounded copy of 11.8 km, which POL-RD-01 forbids citing for the threshold test. Excess = 6.65 km, which is 130.39% of the optimal route and 6.65 km in absolute terms: both POL-RD-01 limbs pass, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED, and the percentage also makes it an additionally MATERIAL deviation.

WHY NO EXCUSE APPLIES. The driver's account that the direct road was heavy is a general traffic assertion with no advisory behind it. POL-RD-08 provides that such an assertion does not discharge the driver's burden, and the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00514-01 is MISSING from the pool (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — no advisory covers the optimal corridor). POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run at all, and the excess is not exonerated. A MISSING artifact can carry no fact; only its absence is citable. The chat log EV-CHAT-00514 contains zero messages, so there is no rider-requested detour and no waypoint_hint to test (POL-RD-04 unavailable). Neither endpoint moved — pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null — so POL-RD-05 does not re-baseline the trip. vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply.

THE REMEDY. Because fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, POL-RD-11 does not bite and POL-RD-02 governs: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 5.1 optimal km + 0.28 x 9.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge multiplier, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, + 0.80 platform fee = 10.945. Charged_total was 19.61. Refund = 19.61 - 10.945 = 8.665, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 8.70. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 44.19% of the charge, below the 90% share that would convert the outcome to a full refund. So the ruling is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.70, and the balance of SGD 10.91 is left in place.

NOTHING IS ADDED OR TAKEN AWAY FOR PASS-THROUGH LINES. The fare breakdown shows no ERP gantries, tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00 and waiting_time_fee 0.00, so POL-RD-09 gives no separate correction and the POL-RD-02 figure is not augmented.

POL-RD-06 WAS RUN, as the MATERIAL deviation requires. The driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 across completed_trips_90d of 250, so no repeat pattern is established: no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The rider's profile likewise raises no premium-corroboration trigger, deviation_claims_60d being 0.

To the rider: the full 19.61 is not refundable, because you did travel the distance; only the distance and time above your booked optimal route is returned. Your point that the trip was fulfilled by a partner fleet does not change the arithmetic — the fare was billed on this platform's meter and POL-RD-02 measures the same lines whoever drove. To the driver: the excess is not excused on this record; to be exonerated for a bad road you would need a traffic advisory naming a road the optimal route uses, with a validity window overlapping the trip, and route evidence showing the vehicle left and rejoined that corridor.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
